organs.label: Roots & rhizomes
organs.summary: Digging up underground parts usually kills the plant or the dug part, so harvest falls directly on survival.

methods.label: Whole-plant digging
methods.note: Removes the individual. Effect depends on which sizes are dug.
measure: share of plants dug per size class
seedling and juvenile counts after harvest

methods.label: Partial rhizome cutting, replanting the crown
methods.note: Leaves part of the rhizome to regrow; regrowth must be checked, not assumed.
measure: regrowth of cut plants the next season
time to reach harvestable size again

organs.label: Bark
organs.process: survival and growth of established plants
organs.summary: Bark stripping wounds the tree. Large trees carry most of the population's growth, so their survival matters most.

methods.label: Strip panels from opposite sides
methods.note: CITES guidance for Prunus africana discusses harvesting opposing quarters so the tree can recover between harvests.

methods.label: Girdling or full stripping
methods.note: Removing bark all round the stem usually kills the tree.

methods.label: Felling then stripping
methods.note: Kills the tree; only regeneration replaces it.

organs.label: Resin & latex (tapping)
organs.summary: Tapping diverts the tree's resources. In Boswellia, tapped trees produced fewer flowers, fruits and seeds.

methods.label: Stem tapping (incisions)
methods.note: Rijkers et al. 2006 found tapping reduced flower, fruit and seed production.
measure: flowering and seed set of tapped vs untapped trees

methods.label: Resting periods between tapping seasons
methods.note: Whether rest restores seed set must be measured locally.
measure: seed set after a rest year

organs.label: Leaves & fronds
organs.summary: Leaf harvest mostly slows growth. A palm study found leaf harvest did not change population growth rate.

methods.label: Partial leaf removal, leaving the growing point
methods.note: Martínez-Ballesté & Martorell 2015 report no effect of leaf harvest on λ for Sabal yapa in homegardens.
measure: new leaves per plant per year

organs.label: Flowers
organs.summary: Taking flowers removes next year's seed. The cost depends on how much the population relies on seed.

methods.label: Picking flower heads
methods.note: Leaving a share of flowers for seed is common practice; the share is not given here.

refs.title: Ticktin T (2004) The ecological implications of harvesting non-timber forest products. J Appl Ecol 41:11–21

organs.label: Fruits & seeds
organs.summary: Fruit and seed harvest reduces recruitment. Long-lived plants often depend little on new seedlings; short-lived ones depend a lot.

methods.label: Collecting fallen fruit
methods.note: Does not harm the parent, but takes seed out of the system.
measure: seedling recruitment in harvested vs unharvested areas

methods.label: Cutting branches to reach fruit
methods.note: Damages the parent as well as removing seed.

refs.title: Ticktin T (2004) The ecological implications of harvesting non-timber forest products. J Appl Ecol 41:11–21

organs.label: Whole herb
organs.summary: Harvesting the whole above-ground plant or uprooting it falls on survival and, before seeding, on reproduction.
